page: Amazon Web Services m7a.48xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs using the AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, and network connectivity delivers a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10%. The DDR5 memory subsystem achieves top-tier read and write bandwidth, particularly in large block uncached operations. Cryptographic and vector instruction workloads perform exceptionally well due to hardware support for AVX-512 and AES extensions. However, single-core performance is comparatively moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the middle 50%. Additionally, while LLM prompt processing speeds are in the top 10%, text generation speeds for smaller models fall into the bottom 25%.

Given its high resource density and dedicated physical cores, the m7a.48xlarge offers high compute and memory throughput for large-scale parallel workloads. It is highly suitable for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, ray tracing, Redis database operations, and high-throughput static web serving. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which should be factored into the architectural design for I/O-heavy database workloads.
